acceptedFindings.title: Predictor and outcome are undefined
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without clinical or operational definitions of 'pred_score' and 'outcome_binary', the discrimination metrics are meaningless to readers and cannot support any clinical interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide clear definitions including the source, derivation, units, and clinical meaning for the risk score, and define the binary outcome event, measurement method, and prevalence.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Verify that the Variables section of the manuscript contains explicit, non-generic descriptions for each variable.

acceptedFindings.title: Risk score derivation not described; possible apparent performance evaluation
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md Variables section: 'Exposure or predictor: pred_score' with no origin
stats-run.json estimates only show term 'pred_score' without origin
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: If pred_score is from a model fit to these same 240 records, the reported AUROC is apparent and overoptimistic, invalidating generalizability and internal evidence claims.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Clarify whether pred_score is an external pre-existing score or derived from the same data. If derived, use cross-validation or an independent test set and report validated performance. If pre-existing, state source.

acceptedFindings.title: No calibration assessment performed
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: For a prediction model evaluation, calibration is as important as discrimination; a well-discriminating but miscalibrated model can produce dangerously misleading risk estimates.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add calibration evaluation: calibration plot, calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, and optionally Hosmer-Lemeshow test; report these metrics alongside AUROC.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the artifact diagnostics.json or output files contain calibration metrics and a calibration plot figure.

acceptedFindings.title: Cohort construction is opaque
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Generalizability, potential selection bias, and data quality cannot be assessed without knowing data source, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and how the 240 complete-cases were obtained.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Describe the data source, study period, eligibility criteria, exclusion steps (e.g., via a flow chart), and any missing data handling; link to a cohort definition artifact.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the manuscript or a referenced cohort artifact contains a step-by-step construction flow and raw case counts.

acceptedFindings.title: AUROC reported without confidence interval
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a confidence interval, the precision of the discrimination estimate is unknown; it is impossible to judge whether the model performs better than chance or acceptably for clinical use.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report a 95% confidence interval for the AUROC (e.g., DeLong method or bootstrap), and include it in both stats-run output and manuscript.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the estimates artifact or manuscript contains an AUROC confidence interval field.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript uses placeholder language and lacks substantive content
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript reads as a generic template: methods state 'cohort definition was read from available run artifacts', discussion is boilerplate, and no concrete clinical context is provided. This fails to communicate the study effectively.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Rewrite the manuscript to include: Background with clinical rationale, detailed Methods with source and cohort specifics, Results with confidence intervals and calibration, Discussion interpreting the findings in context, and focused Limitations.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the manuscript contains sections with specific, non-canned text including references to actual data source, variable definitions, and numeric results beyond the reported metrics.

acceptedFindings.title: No confidence intervals or standard errors for AUROC and Brier score
evidenceRefs: stats-run.json estimates: only point values for auroc and brier_score
manuscript results: 'AUROC was 0.7451 and Brier score was 0.1925'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without CIs, the precision of performance estimates is unknown; the point estimate alone cannot support robust conclusions.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report 95% confidence intervals for AUROC (e.g., DeLong method) and Brier score (e.g., bootstrap). Include in manuscript results.

acceptedFindings.title: No calibration plot or calibration metrics beyond Brier
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: A risk score may discriminate well but be miscalibrated; Brier alone is insufficient. Calibration is essential for clinical utility.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide calibration plot, calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, and ideally a calibration test (e.g., Hosmer-Lemeshow or Spiegelhalter). Add to diagnostics or manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: No description of missing data mechanism or completeness pattern
evidenceRefs: manuscript: 'complete-case sample size was 240' but no missingness analysis
stats-run.json: rowCount=240, completeCaseN=240, no missingness info
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: If missing data are non-ignorable, complete-case analysis can bias performance estimates. The limitation statement is generic and not evidence-based.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Describe original sample size, missingness per variable, pattern, and either justify complete-case (e.g., low missingness <5%) or use appropriate handling (multiple imputation), with sensitivity analysis.

acceptedFindings.title: No analysis code or software details to reproduce the evaluation
evidenceRefs: manuscript Methods: only 'prediction-evaluation' method family, no code/software
stats-run.json lists artifacts but no source code files
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without code, the results are not verifiable, undermining the reproducibility claim in the manuscript.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide the exact computational script (e.g., R/Python) with seeds (if any) and report software versions (e.g., pROC, scikit-learn). Include as supplementary artifact or appendix.

acceptedFindings.title: Brier score lacks interpretative context
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: A Brier score of 0.1925 is difficult to judge without knowing outcome prevalence or a null-model Brier score; readers cannot assess the magnitude of improvement over a naive prediction.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report outcome prevalence and either the Brier skill score (scaled by maximum possible Brier) or the Brier score of a non-informative model (e.g., predicting the mean).
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the manuscript or stats-run summary includes prevalence and a normalized Brier metric.

acceptedFindings.title: Manuscript QA artifact content not provided
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The review packet lists manuscript-qa.json but omits its content; we cannot verify that manuscript-level QA checks (consistency, claim alignment) were performed and passed.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Include the content of manuscript-qa.json in the review packet for the next review cycle.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check that the artifact packet contains a non-empty manuscript-qa.json with a status field.

acceptedFindings.title: ROC curve figure not referenced in manuscript text
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The available ROC curve could aid interpretation, but it is not mentioned in the results or discussion, reducing the report's completeness.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a sentence in the Results section describing the ROC curve and referencing the figure, and include the figure in the manuscript or appendix.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Search the manuscript text for 'ROC' or 'Figure' to confirm presence of the reference.

acceptedFindings.title: Outcome prevalence and pred_score distribution not reported
evidenceRefs: manuscript results: only sample size and metrics
no summary statistics for outcome_binary or pred_score
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Prevalence affects interpretation of Brier score (e.g., null model Brier) and clinical context. Distribution of pred_score influences calibration interpretation.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the proportion of positive outcomes and summary statistics (min, max, mean, sd) of pred_score.

acceptedFindings.title: No comparison to existing risk scores or benchmarks
evidenceRefs: manuscript Introduction and Discussion lack any references
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Even internal evidence should be contextualized to show its novelty and validity relative to known scores for the same outcome.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a brief literature review of relevant risk scores and their reported performance; discuss how the local finding compares.

acceptedFindings.title: No checks reported for predictor distribution or outcome coding
evidenceRefs: stats-qa.json checks do not include data range or coding verification
manuscript no data description beyond variable list
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Unusual values (e.g., negative probabilities, non-0/1 outcome) could distort performance metrics.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Perform and report basic data quality checks: range of pred_score, count of outcome levels, missingness, and any irregularities.
